newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas firms as traders eye arb.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas firms as traders eye arb.

text.p: Singapore gasoline prices on Monday firmed on the back of the strong Western markets as traders eyed the opening arbitrage window, but some traders said exports are unlikely amid regional demand.
Unleaded gasoline in Northwest Europe has risen nearly $30 per tonne from $190 over the past two weeks amid cracker shutdowns, tight prompt supplies and surging U.S. demand.
A European major bid for unleaded 97-octane lifting August 19-23 at $24.60 per barrel fob Singapore.
"Singapore looks cheap compared to the West," said the seller.
On Friday, the fob market was under pressure from two sellers of 92 and 95-octane at $22.30 and $23.25 respectively.
"The arbitrage is not that wide open. Maybe if the West strengthens further, we will see cargoes leaving" a trader said.
"I don't see any cargoes really moving to the West," said one trader. "The market is pretty balanced."
Traders said high-octane gasoline was tight in the region, with exceptional demand from the Philippines adding to the bullish sentiment.
Philippines oil refiner Petron Corp awarded a tender to buy up to 100,000-barrels of 95-octane gasoline for August 10-20 and is seeking another cargo for early September delivery, traders said.
South Korean refiner Ssangyong Oil Refining Co was awarded the August tender which closed last week, at less than $5 per barrel over Singapore naphtha quotes, c-and-f Bataan, traders said.
The tender for the early September delivery cargo closes August 4 and is valid until late August 5, they said.

Petron, which operates a 155,000-bpd refinery in Bataan, north of the capital Manila, had not issued a gasoline import tender since 1995 but had to re-emerge to buy due to increased domestic demand, an official had said.

The August import requirement was also due to the unexpected shutdown of a 15,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) thermal cracker on June 20 following an explosion, while the September requirement is due to a shortfall during the turnaround of a 85,000-bpd crude distillation unit No.2 and 17,000-bpd reformer September 1-12, traders said.
Some trader also said they were waiting for Taiwan's reissued buy tender to close next week on August 11, before looking at the arbitrage.
Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) re-issued a tender to buy 250,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded reformate for September 1-30 delivery, a company official said.
The official did not specify how many cargoes CPC plans to buy in the new tender which seeks cargoes for the full month.
"It is subject on the number," he said. "If it is good we may take more than one, if it is still too high, we may cancel."
CPC last week cancelled its bi-monthly tender to buy reformate for September 1-15 due to high offers.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
